verdict.stance: Neutral / SA Guarantee-Anchored Rail & Port Monopolist Ahead of 2028 Maturity (Ba3)
verdict.summary: Transnet returned to R4.6bn net profit in FY26 (Mar-26) on R88.6bn revenue (+7.1%) and R30.9bn EBITDA, aided by the Durban Pier 2 49.999% stake sale to ICTSI. Standalone metrics remain stretched (R136bn+ debt, R23.3bn capex, 49.5% gearing vs 50% covenant ceiling), but R51bn–R99.6bn South African government guarantee frameworks backstop debt service and Feb-2028 $1bn Eurobond refinancing.

positives: Explicit South African National Treasury guarantee framework (R51bn–R99.6bn) covering multi-year redemptions.
Strategic rail and port monopoly; ICTSI Durban Pier 2 JV monetization lifted FY26 profit to R4.6bn.
Moody's Ba3 CFR anchored by extraordinary state support.
negatives: Weak standalone BCA (caa1/b3): ~R136bn+ gross debt, R23.3bn capex, and razor-thin 49.5% gearing vs 50% covenant cap.
Rail freight volume recovery remains gradual despite tariff increases.
$1.0bn 8.25% Eurobond bullet maturity approaches in Feb-2028.

background.business_overview: South Africa's 100% state-owned rail freight, port terminal, and fuel pipeline monopoly.
background.asset_perimeter: Transnet Freight Rail, Transnet National Ports Authority, Transnet Port Terminals (incl. Durban Pier 2 JV), Pipelines.

recent_drivers: FY26 (Mar-26): Revenue R88.6bn (+7.1%), EBITDA R30.9bn, NPAT R4.6bn (Durban Pier 2 49.999% sale to ICTSI), capex R23.3bn, gearing 49.5%.
2025-26: SA government formalized R51bn guarantee facility & up to ~R99.6bn multi-year guarantee framework.
